facts.statement: Gulosaurus was first described by Cuthbertson, Russell, and Anderson in 2013.
facts.quote: Gulosaurus was first named by Robin S. Cuthbertson, Anthony P. Russell and Jason S. Anderson in 2013

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Gulosaurus is Gulosaurus helmi.
facts.quote: the type species is Gulosaurus helmi

facts.statement: Fossils of Gulosaurus have been found in the Early Triassic Vega-Phroso Siltstone Member of the Sulphur Mountain Formation in east-central British Columbia, Canada.
facts.quote: known from the Early Triassic Vega-Phroso Siltstone Member of the Sulphur Mountain Formation of east-central British Columbia, Canada

facts.statement: The name Gulosaurus translates to 'Helm's wolverine lizard'.
Initially, the incomplete fossil was thought to belong to either Grippia longirostris or Parvinatator wapitiensis.
facts.quote: Originally Gulosaurus was thought to be either Grippia longirostris or Parvinatator wapitiensis, but as the fossil was incomplete it was uncertain which

facts.statement: The discovery of the missing half of the fossil, including the skull, in 2013 confirmed Gulosaurus as a distinct new species.
facts.quote: In 2013, the other half of the fossil, including its skull, was discovered and this proved it to be a new species entirely

facts.statement: Gulosaurus grew to a length of approximately 1.5 meters.
facts.quote: It was the same size, around 1.5 meters long

facts.statement: Unlike many later ichthyopterygians, Gulosaurus possessed pentadactyl limbs instead of polyphalangy.
facts.quote: it had pentadactyl limbs rather than exhibiting polyphalangy, as many later ichthyopterygians did

facts.statement: The flipper structure of Gulosaurus was similar to Grippia, except the first metacarpal had a notched peripheral shaft rather than a lunate shape.
facts.quote: Most of the flipper structure was very similar apart from the first metacarpal, which had a notched peripheral shaft in Gulosaurus but was lunate in Grippia

facts.statement: Gulosaurus had a skull with cylindrical anterior teeth, differing from Grippia.
facts.quote: The skull of Gulosaurus was also very different to that of Grippia - it had cylindrical anterior teeth

facts.statement: Gulosaurus is classified as an extinct genus of basal grippidian ichthyopterygian.
facts.quote: Gulosaurus is an extinct genus of basal grippidian ichthyopterygian

facts.statement: The parent group of Gulosaurus is Grippidia.
Gulosaurus belongs to the class Reptilia.

rejected.statement: The skull of Gulosaurus showed postfrontal-frontal contact at the rostral limit of the anterior margin of the supratemporal terrace.
rejected.quote: The skull also exhibited postfrontal-frontal contact at the rostral limit of the anterior margin of the supratemporal terrace
